proposition: Nafsat I asserts that Ibn Turka studied 25 years under his elder brother in a family that had served the religious sciences for two centuries, then 15 years abroad at his teachers' direction, and that in all that time he studied only tafsir, hadith, uṣūl al-dīn and jurisprudence, never neglecting the Sharīʿa. This is his own self-presentation to Shāhrukh.

mediation.who: Ibn Turka, writing to the ruler who was judging him
Melvin-Koushki, The Quest for a Universal Science (Yale 2012)
